messages:

To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing & packaging question

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team was impressed with the latencies on shorter sequences. We're evaluating a 12-month pilot that would include a Dedicated pool for model inference and a Private control plane integration. Before we loop procurement, can you share a rough ballpark for committed capacity pricing and whether you offer any bundling (e.g., reserved nodes + support + longer-term model pinning discounts)?

I've attached our initial requirements (high level). We expect ~3M tokens/month initially, with a growth runway to ~9M tokens/month by Q4.

Best,
Emma

Hi Emma — really appreciate the clear requirements. I copied Ben (AE) and Lauren (VP Sales) to start a proposal.

High-level: we can propose a 12-month reserved capacity package with a committed minimum (covers the 3M baseline) and defined burst credits for projected growth. There are a few levers we typically use to get unit economics where customers want them: upfront prepayment, higher commit, and adjustments to retention/archival policies.

Ben — can you draft a pilot package and call out the approval path if we need to go beyond standard pricing thresholds? Emma — we'll aim to get a draft to you by EOD.

Thanks,

Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: VectorHealth draft: recommended commercial package (internal)

Team — attaching a draft proposal I plan to send to VectorHealth. Key commercial ask from them is a 12-month pilot with predictable spend; they want a meaningful discount compared to list since they will commit to reserved capacity plus private deployment costs.

Proposed commercial structure (draft):
- 12-month committed reserved Dedicated compute equivalent to 4 baseline GPUs (16 vGPU units)
- Monthly baseline: 3M tokens (growing to 9M by month 6); included burst pool for +30% at 2x unit rate
- Professional services: one-time onboarding fee waived if customer prepays first 6 months
- Proposed discount: 40–45% off published hosted API list, applied to committed capacity and private control plane fees.
- Trade-offs to tighten economics if needed: reduce retention from 90 days to 30 days, require annual prepay, or set a minimum 18-month commit for 45%

Why we need escalation: our standard delegated discount cap for AE is 25% for this packaging. Anything beyond that requires VP/CFO sign-off due to margin and revenue recognition implications. Asking for an exception to approve up to 45% if customer commits to prepay and an 18-month extension.

Attachments: VectorHealth_MAAP_proposal_v1.pdf, RDW_SOW_VectorHealth_draft.docx

Can Marissa or Lauren confirm whether finance is ok to proceed with a 40% exception if the customer prepays 6 months? If not, what floor should we use to stay within acceptable unit economics?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: VectorHealth_MAAP_proposal_v1.pdf (application/pdf), RDW_SOW_VectorHealth_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VectorHealth draft: recommended commercial package (internal)

Agree with Ben's structure. A couple of negotiation notes before we request formal sign-off:
- Aim for 40% as a baseline ask, keep 45% as an overhang if they agree to 18 months + annual prepay.
- If finance pushes back, trade on SLA windows (standard latency SLO vs premium) and retention rather than price — VectorHealth cares most about predictability and isolation, less about the few cents per token edge cases.
- We should tie discount approval to a minimum ARR floor ($250k ARR) — below that, we should stay within 30% cap.

Marissa — can you provide an approval threshold memo? Specifically we need: 1) approval to offer 40% with 6-month prepay, or 2) confirmation that 45% requires CFO/VP sign-off plus prepay + 18 months. I can then send the external-facing proposal and mark it "subject to financial approval."

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VectorHealth draft: recommended commercial package (internal)

Thanks — I looked through the numbers in the dump. Before I sign off on any exception, I need the following explicitly called out in a short memo:
1) ARR impact and month-by-month cashflow given proposed prepay options (6-mo vs 18-mo).
2) Unit economics: expected gross margin at 40% and 45% (assume current cost-per-token baseline).
3) Cancellation/rollback clause: if usage growth doesn't materialize, what's the minimum commitment and any make-good/clawback?
4) Risk mitigations: operational responsibilities for Private deployment + who owns escalation support (CS vs Solutions).

Ben — can you produce a one-page exception memo (bullet list + numbers) and put the recommended fallback pricing if we can only approve 30%? Attach to this thread and I'll review. I can move quickly if the memo includes the numbers.

Marissa Cole
CFO, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 12:00:00 -0700
Subject: VectorHealth exception memo for VP/CFO sign-off — request

Marissa — attaching the one-page exception memo and the updated proposal for your quick review. Summary below so you don't need to open attachments: 

Executive ask: Approve a commercial exception to permit up to 40% discount for a 12-month reserved pilot if VectorHealth prepays 6 months; authorize up to 45% only if they agree to an 18-month committed term and annual prepayment.

Key numbers (summarized):
- Committed baseline: 3M tokens/month; price at list = $0.0008/token => baseline monthly list = $2,400; applied to reserved node equivalent + private control plane markup -> effective list-equivalent monthly = $32,000 (includes infra & support).
- Proposed 40% discount => effective monthly = $19,200; annualized ARR = $230,400 (12 months).
- Proposed 45% with 18-month commit & annual prepay => effective monthly = $17,600; 18-month cashflow delivered upfront if annual prepay chosen.
- Gross margin estimate: ~52% at 40% discount; ~47% at 45% discount (current cost assumptions).
- Minimum ARR floor for the exception: $200k committed ARR.
- Cancellation: pro-rated refund only on unused prepaid months, with 60-day notice and a 10% early termination fee to protect unit economics.
- Operational: Solutions to own onboarding timeline (30-day SLA), CS owns post-go-live SLAs; private deployment runbook attached.

Attachments: Exception_memo_VectorHealth_1p.pdf, VectorHealth_MAAP_proposal_v1.pdf, RDW_SOW_VectorHealth_draft.docx
DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/packet/abc123

Request: Marissa / Lauren — please reply with APPROVE / DECLINE or REQUEST CHANGES. If APPROVE, I will mark the external proposal as "Finance approved" and proceed to send to Emma + procurement.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: Exception_memo_VectorHealth_1p.pdf (application/pdf)]
